groups.title: General

groups.desc: Several people on this server hear the same songs at the same time, each on their own device. Anyone signed in can start one and invite others with a code or a link.

fields.help: Off hides every group listen entry in the apps and ends the ones that are running
fields.label: Allow group listens

fields.help: The host also switches “Guests can join with the link” on for their group; both must be on. Guests listen on a web page: they can't add songs or control playback, and nothing they hear is logged or scrobbled. Their access ends with the group, when they leave, or after 12 hours.
fields.label: Let people without an account join with the invite link

fields.help: Guests count too. A host can set a lower limit for their group.
fields.label: Most people in one group listen

fields.help: They come back paused where they were, the apps join again by themselves and the host presses play. Off: a restart ends them. Group listens nobody used for 12 hours end either way.
fields.label: Keep group listens through a server restart

groups.title: Group listens

groups.desc: Encore copies its database once a day and before every upgrade (config/backups, or .encore-backups in the music folder when the config disk is full). Older copies are deleted at every start and after every backup; uploaded backups are never deleted.

fields.help: Copies kept in all, shared out daily, weekly and monthly: 3 is the newest, one from an earlier week and one from an earlier month; 6 is two of each.
fields.label: Backups to keep

fields.help: The copies taken just before an upgrade (to go back to the older Encore), kept besides the ones above.
fields.label: Pre-upgrade copies to keep

groups.title: Database backups

groups.desc: Listens to each download and checks it's really the song you asked for, not a remix, live or wrong track.

groups.title: Verification & duplicates

groups.desc: Where translated and romanized titles come from, strongest first: corrections by hand, official names, romanization built into the server, DeepL with your API key, and the local model when the Translator plugin is installed. Each listener turns translations on under Settings → Language, which also shows admins the state of each source.

fields.help: MusicBrainz pseudo-releases and aliases, and Apple's English names for Japanese releases. Asks MusicBrainz and Apple about the songs in your library.
fields.label: Official names from MusicBrainz and Apple

fields.help: Japanese kana, Korean, Cyrillic, Greek, Hebrew, Arabic, Thai and Devanagari, made on this server. Titles with kanji and Chinese titles are left to the other sources.
fields.label: Romanization built into the server

fields.help: Translates song and album titles, never lyrics or artist names.
fields.label: DeepL, when an API key is set

fields.help: From deepl.com → Account → API keys. A key ending in :fx is a free-plan key (500,000 characters a month at DeepL).
fields.label: DeepL API key

fields.help: Encore stops asking DeepL for the rest of the month at this many characters. 0 = no limit.
fields.label: DeepL characters per month

fields.help: Translates and romanizes what the other sources leave, on this server, with the Translator plugin (llama.cpp and a model). It is not installed by default: install the Translator in Plugins.
fields.label: Local model, when it is installed

groups.title: Translated titles

groups.desc: Dolby Atmos and other 5.1 and 7.1 versions of songs, in a Surround library of their own: never in the stereo lists, shuffle, playlists or stats. Admins fetch an album's or a song's Atmos version from its page (gamdl with a wrapper-v2 server); a surround file a normal request downloads lands here too. Kodi, Plex or Jellyfin can read the folder as a library of its own.

fields.help: Where surround versions are filed. Empty: Surround inside the music library path (/music/Surround).
fields.label: Surround folder

fields.help: When a song or album request is done and Apple Music has it in Dolby Atmos, its Atmos version is fetched into Surround too. Needs the gamdl plugin with a wrapper-v2 server.
fields.label: Fetch the Dolby Atmos version after each request

fields.help: When the Surround folder is inside the music library, writes .plexignore and .ndignore there so Plex and Navidrome libraries over /music don't show the surround albums twice. Add the Surround folder to them as a library of its own.
fields.label: Hide the Surround folder from stereo media-server libraries

groups.title: Surround (Dolby Atmos)

groups.desc: What happens to a file when you delete an album, a song or a file. Off: it is deleted for good straight away. On: it waits in the Trash (Settings → System → Files → Trash, on the music disk) and can be restored until the days run out.

fields.help: Off: deleting an album, a song or a file deletes it for good. On: it goes to the Trash first, where you can restore it.
fields.label: Keep deleted files in Trash

fields.help: After this many days a file in the Trash is deleted for good (also what a reported song's old file waits once its replacement arrived).
fields.label: Keep them for

groups.title: Deleting files

groups.desc: Which sources are searched for a request, and in what order. The first one that has it wins.

fields.help: The one place to set what is searched, in order, comma-separated: qobuz, tidal, deezer (all through streamrip), slskd (Soulseek), torznab (torrents/Usenet, albums only), ytdlp (YouTube Music). Leave one out to never use it; sources you haven’t set up are skipped. Recommended (the default): qobuz, tidal, deezer, slskd, torznab, ytdlp – exact hi-res/lossless releases first, then Soulseek, then torrents/Usenet for whole albums, YouTube Music last. With Highest quality first on (the default), requests try Qobuz/Tidal/Deezer, then FLAC on Soulseek, then torrents/Usenet, then Soulseek in any format, then YouTube Music.
fields.label: Source order

groups.title: Download pipeline

groups.desc: Which releases Request discography, the artist pages and New releases count, like the metadata profiles in Lidarr. Song requests skip other versions (live, remix, sped up and so on) unless the song asked for is one.

fields.help: Request discography gets these. Each request can change them in its own panel.
fields.label: Kinds to request

fields.help: A release with any ticked extra is left out. Instrumental, acoustic, sped up, karaoke and covers are read from the titles. An artist can have their own: Release types on the artist’s page.
fields.label: Skip releases that are

fields.help: A single whose song is on one of the artist’s studio albums is downloaded with that album instead of on its own (once, even when both are requested). Singles of songs on no album are downloaded as singles.
fields.label: Singles on an album: get the album

groups.title: Release types

groups.desc: Searches the Soulseek file-sharing network – great for FLAC and rare releases. Encore runs Soulseek for you: enter any username and password and an account is created at the first sign-in. Forward the port for the best speeds.

fields.help: New name + password = new account. Don’t use the same login in another Soulseek client at the same time.
fields.label: Soulseek username

fields.help: TCP port Soulseek listens on – forward it on your router (and publish it in Docker) so users behind firewalls can send to you. While Send Soulseek through a VPN is on, the VPN’s forwarded port is used instead.
fields.label: Listen port

fields.help: The network runs on sharing; many users refuse downloads to people who share nothing. Only the library folder is shared, read-only.
fields.label: Share your library on Soulseek (recommended)
Downloads folder (as mounted in this container)

Max users to try per request

fields.label: Send Soulseek through a VPN

fields.help: Paste the whole .conf file from your VPN provider (ProtonVPN: Downloads → WireGuard configuration, with NAT-PMP port forwarding on). The private key is stored on this server only.

groups.title: YouTube Music & links (yt-dlp)

groups.desc: Signs yt-dlp in to YouTube: YouTube Music Premium unlocks 256 kbps audio, and signed-in downloads see fewer bot checks. Best: connect the Encore browser extension and hand over a sign-in from a private window – Encore then owns that session and keeps it alive by itself. Pasted cookies are the backup.

fields.help: Netscape cookie file exported from music.youtube.com. Used only when there is no signed-in hand-off or extension sync. Export from a private window and close it right after, so your own browser does not rotate them.
fields.label: Pasted cookies.txt (backup)

fields.help: Only for pasted cookies while they are in use: Encore renews them the way an open YouTube tab does and saves the new ones. A handed-over sign-in is always refreshed every 4 hours; an everyday browser’s cookies never are (that would sign that browser out).
fields.label: Refresh pasted cookies every 4 hours

groups.title: YouTube sign-in

groups.desc: API keys that let users connect their Spotify, Tidal, Last.fm, Discogs and YouTube Music accounts, and power recommendations.

fields.help: developer.spotify.com – add <Public URL>/api/connections/spotify/callback as redirect URI. Development-mode apps allow 5 users and need a Premium owner (2026 rules); without it, public playlists still import via the embed fallback.
fields.label: Spotify Client ID

fields.help: Only for looking up Tidal albums/songs by ISRC and for the Tidal connection. Get one at developer.tidal.com → Dashboard → Create new app (any name), redirect URI <Public URL>/api/connections/tidal/callback, then copy the Client ID and Client secret here. Downloads from Tidal use your own account instead: Plugins → streamrip → Sign in to Tidal.
fields.label: Tidal Client ID

fields.help: last.fm/api/account/create (free) – loved tracks, similar artists/songs, genre pages, For you
fields.label: Last.fm API key

fields.help: Shown next to the API key. Needed for scrobbling: users sign in with Last.fm on the Connections page.
fields.label: Last.fm shared secret

fields.help: discogs.com/settings/developers → “Generate new token” and paste that personal access token here (not an application’s Consumer Key/Secret – no app is needed). Finds vinyl, bootlegs and old releases MusicBrainz is missing.
fields.label: Discogs personal access token

fields.help: Google Cloud → YouTube Data API v3 → OAuth client of type “TVs and Limited Input devices”. Lets users sign in to YouTube Music with a code (they can also paste browser headers instead).
fields.label: YouTube Music OAuth Client ID

fields.help: Each song is rendered once and kept on disk, so seeking and skipping need no new processing and the next song is ready before it plays. The least recently played renders make room. 0 = no cache (every stream is processed live).
